Description: 146 garment workers, mostly young immigrant women, died in a NYC factory fire; exit doors had been locked to prevent theft.
Structural_Note: Private employer imposed a physical risk the workforce could not exit; no external safety floor applied.
Sources: The Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire (U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration) <https://www.osha.gov/aboutosha/40-years/trianglefactoryfire> ; Triangle shirtwaist factory fire (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Triangle-shirtwaist-factory-fire>

Authority: Colorado National Guard & Colorado Fuel & Iron Co. (its controlling family)
Description: Guardsmen and company guards attacked a striking miners' tent colony in Colorado; about 21 died, including two women and eleven children.
Structural_Note: State force deployed on behalf of a private authority against a non-consenting population.
Sources: Ludlow Massacre (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Ludlow-Massacre> ; Ludlow Massacre (Colorado Encyclopedia) <https://coloradoencyclopedia.org/article/ludlow-massacre>

Authority: Municipal officials and police in multiple US cities
Description: White mobs attacked Black communities across dozens of US cities; police often failed to protect Black residents; hundreds killed.
Structural_Note: Public authority did not act to protect a population it was responsible for; private violence proceeded unchecked.
Sources: Racial Violence and the Red Summer (U.S. National Archives) <https://www.archives.gov/research/african-americans/wwi/red-summer> ; Red Summer of 1919: How Black WWI Vets Fought Back Against Racist Mobs (HISTORY) <https://www.history.com/articles/red-summer-1919-riots-chicago-dc-great-migration>

Authority: Tulsa city officials and deputized police
Description: A white mob, hundreds of them deputized by police, destroyed the prosperous Black Greenwood district; estimates run to hundreds killed and thousands displaced.
Structural_Note: Public authority deputized participants; the affected community had no protection from the authority meant to provide it.
Sources: Justice Department Announces Results of Review and Evaluation of the Tulsa Race Massacre (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-announces-results-review-and-evaluation-tulsa-race-massacre> ; The 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre (Oklahoma Historical Society) <https://www.okhistory.org/learn/tulsaracemassacre>

Description: Tetraethyl lead was added to gasoline despite known toxicity; refinery workers died of lead poisoning in the 1920s and population-wide lead exposure persisted for decades until phase-out.
Structural_Note: A population-wide exposure was introduced without the consent of those exposed; once dispersed it was not reversible.
Sources: Leaded Gas Was a Known Poison the Day It Was Invented (Smithsonian Magazine) <https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/leaded-gas-poison-invented-180961368/> ; Lead Poisoning: A Historical Perspective (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency) <https://www.epa.gov/archive/epa/aboutepa/lead-poisoning-historical-perspective.html>

Authority: Commonwealth of Virginia / U.S. Supreme Court
Description: SCOTUS upheld compulsory sterilization of those deemed 'unfit'; the ruling enabled roughly 70,000 forced sterilizations across the states over subsequent decades.
Structural_Note: Judicial authorization for state control over the bodies of a non-consenting class; the ruling bound later cases.
Sources: U.S. Reports: Buck v. Bell, 274 U.S. 200 (1927) (Library of Congress) <https://www.loc.gov/item/usrep274200/> ; The Supreme Court Ruling That Led To 70,000 Forced Sterilizations (NPR Fresh Air, via WUNC) <https://www.wunc.org/2016-03-07/the-supreme-court-ruling-that-led-to-70-000-forced-sterilizations>

Description: Federal researchers withheld treatment from hundreds of Black men with syphilis to study the disease's progression, continuing even after penicillin became standard; ran until 1972.
Structural_Note: Public research authority withheld an available treatment from non-consenting subjects, who could not see or stop the program.
Sources: The Untreated Syphilis Study at Tuskegee Timeline (U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) <https://www.cdc.gov/tuskegee/about/timeline.html>

Description: Federal troops used cavalry, tanks, and gas to clear WWI veterans and families demanding promised bonuses from encampments in Washington, DC.
Structural_Note: Military force used against citizens petitioning the government.
Sources: The 1932 Bonus Army (U.S. National Park Service) <https://www.nps.gov/articles/the-1932-bonus-army.htm> ; Bonus Army (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Bonus-Army>

Description: About 120,000 people of Japanese descent, most U.S. citizens, were forcibly removed from their homes and held in camps without charge.
Structural_Note: Mass deprivation of liberty and property of a class defined by ancestry, without charge; later formally redressed by Congress.
Sources: Japanese-American Incarceration During World War II (U.S. National Archives) <https://www.archives.gov/education/lessons/japanese-relocation> ; Executive Order 9066 (U.S. National Park Service) <https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/executive-order-9066.htm>

Authority: U.S. Atomic Energy Commission and predecessors
Description: Government-sponsored researchers exposed uninformed patients, soldiers, and others to radiation, including plutonium injections, beginning in the 1940s.
Structural_Note: State conducted nonconsensual experiments; subjects could neither see nor stop them.
Sources: Final Report of the Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments: Executive Summary (U.S. Department of Energy) <https://ehss.energy.gov/ohre/roadmap/achre/summary.html> ; ACHRE Report, Chapter 5: The Manhattan District Experiments (U.S. Department of Energy) <https://ehss.energy.gov/ohre/roadmap/achre/chap5_2.html>

Authority: U.S. Steel (American Steel & Wire / zinc works)
Description: Industrial emissions trapped by a temperature inversion killed about 20 people and sickened thousands in Donora, Pennsylvania.
Structural_Note: Industrial emissions imposed acute harm on a host community with no means to halt them.
Sources: The Deadly Donora Smog of 1948 Spurred Environmental Protection (Smithsonian Magazine) <https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/deadly-donora-smog-1948-spurred-environmental-protection-have-we-forgotten-lesson-180970533/> ; Smog Deaths In 1948 Led To Clean Air Laws (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=103359330>

Description: The CIA secretly administered drugs including LSD to unwitting subjects and funded coercive experiments; the program ran until 1964 (with follow-on projects after), and its records were largely destroyed in 1973.
Structural_Note: Covert state experimentation on non-consenting individuals; records were later destroyed, limiting external review.
Sources: Project MKULTRA, the CIA's Program of Research in Behavioral Modification, joint Senate hearing, 1977 (U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence) <https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/sites-default-files-hearings-95mkultra.pdf> ; MK-ULTRA (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/MK-ULTRA>

Description: A federal campaign deported large numbers of Mexican nationals, with U.S. citizens of Mexican descent also detained and removed in the sweeps.
Structural_Note: Enforcement action removed individuals, including citizens, without individualized due process.
Sources: The Largest Mass Deportation in American History (HISTORY) <https://www.history.com/articles/operation-wetback-eisenhower-1954-deportation> ; Operation Wetback (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/Operation-Wetback>

Description: The FBI ran covert programs to surveil, infiltrate, and disrupt civil-rights, anti-war, and political organizations, including unlawful tactics; exposed 1971.
Structural_Note: Domestic intelligence authority directed at lawful political activity.
Sources: COINTELPRO (FBI Records: The Vault, Federal Bureau of Investigation) <https://vault.fbi.gov/cointel-pro> ; COINTELPRO (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/COINTELPRO>

Description: The heavily polluted Cuyahoga River in Cleveland, Ohio caught fire; one of several such fires, it became a national symbol of unregulated industrial discharge.
Structural_Note: A shared commons was degraded by industrial discharge whose cost fell on the public rather than the discharger.
Sources: Cuyahoga River Fire (Encyclopedia of Cleveland History, Case Western Reserve University) <https://case.edu/ech/articles/c/cuyahoga-river-fire> ; Carl B. Stokes and the 1969 River Fire (U.S. National Park Service) <https://www.nps.gov/articles/carl-stokes-and-the-river-fire.htm>

Description: Guardsmen opened fire on a crowd during an anti-war protest at Kent State University in Ohio, killing four students and wounding nine.
Structural_Note: State force used against unarmed protesters, resulting in deaths.
Sources: Kent State shooting (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Kent-State-shootings> ; The May 4 Shootings at Kent State University: The Search for Historical Accuracy (Kent State University) <https://www.kent.edu/may-4-historical-accuracy>

Description: State forces retook Attica prison by force after a four-day uprising over conditions; 43 people died, most from state gunfire including hostages.
Structural_Note: State force in a custodial setting caused deaths among people in its own custody.
Sources: Massacre at Attica Prison, September 13, 1971 (HISTORY) <https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/september-13/massacre-at-attica-prison> ; Attica Correctional Facility (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/Attica-Correctional-Facility>

Event: Kerr-McGee Plutonium Contamination and Worker Safety Failures
Description: A nuclear-plant worker raising safety and contamination concerns was found contaminated with plutonium and died in a contested car crash; litigation found plant safety failures.
Structural_Note: A worker raising safety concerns was contaminated; litigation found facility safety failures.
Sources: U.S. Supreme Court opinion, 464 U.S. 238 (1984) (Justia) <https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/464/238/> ; Events At Kerr-McGee Highlight Inadequacies Of Plutonium Industry Regulation (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/transcripts/776331685>

Description: Thousands of tons of buried chemical waste contaminated a Niagara Falls, NY neighborhood and school, prompting a federal emergency and relocations.
Structural_Note: Waste disposed without disclosure left an unknowing community exposed; the contamination was not reversible.
Sources: The Love Canal Tragedy (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency) <https://www.epa.gov/archive/epa/aboutepa/love-canal-tragedy.html> ; Love Canal (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/place/Love-Canal>

Description: A partial reactor meltdown in Pennsylvania released radiation and exposed serious operator and regulatory shortcomings.
Structural_Note: Operator and regulator both fell short of the safeguards the surrounding population relied on.
Sources: Backgrounder on the Three Mile Island Accident (U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission) <https://www.nrc.gov/reading-rm/doc-collections/fact-sheets/3mile-isle>

Description: A gas leak at a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India killed thousands and injured hundreds of thousands; safety systems were inadequate.
Structural_Note: A U.S.-headquartered authority's operation imposed catastrophic risk on a foreign host population with no role in the decisions.
Sources: Bhopal disaster (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Bhopal-disaster> ; The Bhopal disaster and its aftermath: a review (Environmental Health, via PubMed Central) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1142333/>

Description: Police dropped an explosive device on a row house occupied by the MOVE group, killing 11 people including 5 children and burning down 61 homes.
Structural_Note: Municipal authority used military-grade force in a residential neighborhood.
Sources: MOVE Bombing (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/MOVE-Bombing> ; MOVE (Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia) <https://philadelphiaencyclopedia.org/essays/move/>

Authority: Thrift industry, federal regulators, and Congress
Description: Deregulation, lax supervision, and in some cases fraud collapsed hundreds of thrifts; the taxpayer cleanup cost roughly $124 billion.
Structural_Note: Private risk-taking was followed by a public-funded backstop; the cost fell on taxpayers.
Sources: Savings and Loan Crisis (Federal Reserve History) <https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/savings-and-loan-crisis> ; The Savings and Loan Crisis and Its Relationship to Banking, History of the Eighties (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) <https://www.fdic.gov/resources/publications/history-eighties/volume-1/history-80s-volume-1-part1-04.pdf>

Description: A tanker ran aground in Prince William Sound, Alaska, spilling about 11 million gallons of crude and devastating the marine ecosystem.
Structural_Note: Coastal commons and dependent communities bore the cost of a private operator's failure.
Sources: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill (NOAA Office of Response and Restoration) <https://response.restoration.noaa.gov/oil-and-chemical-spills/significant-incidents/exxon-valdez-oil-spill> ; Exxon Valdez oil spill (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Exxon-Valdez-oil-spill>

Event: Police beating of a motorist during an arrest
Description: Officers were videotaped beating a man during an arrest; their later acquittal triggered widespread unrest.
Structural_Note: Documented use of force; internal review did not initially produce accountability.
Sources: Los Angeles Riots of 1992 (Britannica Student Encyclopedia) <https://kids.britannica.com/students/article/Los-Angeles-Riots-of-1992/632663> ; Police brutality in the United States (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/police-brutality-in-the-United-States-2307592>

Description: A federal siege in Idaho left a man's wife and son dead; subsequent reviews found rules-of-engagement and oversight failures.
Structural_Note: Federal force resulted in non-combatant deaths; later review found rules-of-engagement violations.
Sources: Report of the Ruby Ridge Task Force, 1994 (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://www.justice.gov/sites/default/files/opr/legacy/2006/11/09/rubyreportcover_39.pdf> ; Ruby Ridge (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Ruby-Ridge>

Description: A 51-day siege of the Branch Davidian compound in Texas ended in a fire; about 76 people died, including children.
Structural_Note: Escalation by federal authority preceded mass loss of life under circumstances still contested.
Sources: Evaluation of the Handling of the Branch Davidian Stand-Off in Waco, Texas (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://www.justice.gov/archives/publications/waco/evaluation-handling-branch-davidian-stand-waco-texas-february-28-april-19-1993> ; Waco siege (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Waco-siege>

Description: Seven tobacco CEOs told Congress they did not believe nicotine was addictive; internal documents later showed the industry knew and concealed addiction and harm.
Structural_Note: Tobacco companies withheld material evidence of addiction and health risks, limiting the public's and regulators' ability to independently assess the dangers.
Sources: Tobacco CEO's Statement to Congress 1994 (University of California, San Francisco) <https://senate.ucsf.edu/tobacco-ceo-statement-to-congress>

Description: Purdue aggressively marketed OxyContin while downplaying addiction risks, contributing to widespread opioid prescribing, dependence, and associated harms.
Structural_Note: Product risks were systematically misrepresented to prescribers and the public.
Sources: The Promotion and Marketing of OxyContin: Commercial Triumph, Public Health Tragedy (American Journal of Public Health, via PubMed Central) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2622774/> ; Origins of the Opioid Crisis and Its Enduring Impacts (via PubMed Central) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9272388/>

Description: Accounting fraud hid massive losses; the firm's collapse wiped out employee retirement savings and destroyed its auditor.
Structural_Note: Falsified accounting, later adjudicated, shifted concealed risk onto employees and investors.
Sources: Enron scandal: Downfall and bankruptcy (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Enron-scandal/Downfall-and-bankruptcy> ; Ex-Employees Fight for Shreds of Enron Pensions (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/2006/05/26/5435098/ex-employees-fight-for-shreds-of-enron-pensions>

Description: Published photographs documented torture and humiliation of detainees by U.S. personnel at a prison in Iraq.
Structural_Note: Custodial authority abused detainees within its power, outside legal limits.
Sources: Abu Ghraib prison (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/topic/Abu-Ghraib-prison> ; Investigation into U.S. Abuse of Iraqi Prisoners (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/2004/05/07/1870746/investigation-into-u-s-abuse-of-iraqi-prisoners>

Authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers / FEMA
Description: Engineered flood-protection systems failed during Katrina, flooding New Orleans; about 1,800 died and the federal response was widely judged inadequate.
Structural_Note: Engineered flood protection and the emergency response both fell short for the population relying on them.
Sources: Hurricane Katrina - August 2005 (National Weather Service) <https://www.weather.gov/mob/katrina> ; Hurricane Katrina: A Nation Still Unprepared, S. Rpt. 109-322 (U.S. Senate, via GovInfo) <https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CRPT-109srpt322/pdf/CRPT-109srpt322.pdf>

Authority: Major banks; SEC and Federal Reserve oversight
Description: Predatory lending and opaque securities triggered the worst crash since the 1930s; millions lost homes and jobs while large institutions were bailed out.
Structural_Note: Concentrated private risk was realized as broad public loss; large institutions received public support.
Sources: Bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/bankruptcy-of-Lehman-Brothers> ; The Financial Crisis Inquiry Report (Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission, via GovInfo) <https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GPO-FCIC/pdf/GPO-FCIC.pdf>

Authority: A Ponzi-scheme operator; SEC supervisory failure
Event: Ponzi Scheme and Regulatory Oversight Failures
Description: A Ponzi scheme that had reported roughly $65 billion in investor accounts collapsed; the SEC had received and dismissed credible warnings for years.
Structural_Note: The regulator received specific, repeated warnings and did not act on them.
Sources: Report of Investigation, Case No. OIG-509, Executive Summary (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of Inspector General) <https://www.sec.gov/spotlight/secpotmadoffrefroms/oig-509-exec-summary.pdf> ; Government memorandum opposing sentence reduction, No. 09 Cr. 213 (S.D.N.Y.), 2020 (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/page/file/1258026/dl>

Description: An explosion at a West Virginia coal mine killed 29 workers; investigators cited systematic safety violations and a culture of concealment.
Structural_Note: Investigators cited systematic safety violations and hazards kept out of official records preceding worker deaths.
Sources: MSHA cites corporate culture as root cause of Upper Big Branch Mine disaster (U.S. Department of Labor) <https://www.dol.gov/newsroom/releases/msha/msha20111206> ; Upper Big Branch Mine-South Fatal Accident Report, Executive Summary (Mine Safety and Health Administration) <https://www.msha.gov/sites/default/files/Data_Reports/Fatals/Coal/Upper%20Big%20Branch/ExecutiveSummary.pdf>

Description: A blowout killed 11 workers and released about 3.2 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico, the largest marine oil spill in U.S. history.
Structural_Note: Failures in well-barrier integrity, interpretation of safety-test results, and operational oversight preceded worker deaths and widespread, persistent ecological harm.
Sources: Deepwater Horizon 10 Years Later: 10 Questions (NOAA Fisheries) <https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/news/deepwater-horizon-10-years-later-10-questions> ; Deepwater Horizon - BP Gulf of America Oil Spill (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency) <https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/deepwater-horizon-bp-gulf-america-oil-spill>

Event: NSA Bulk Surveillance and Failure of Oversight
Description: Leaked documents revealed bulk collection of Americans' phone records and large-scale internet surveillance; a federal appeals court later ruled the bulk phone-records program exceeded its statutory authority.
Structural_Note: Bulk collection of the general population's phone records, later ruled by an appeals court to exceed statutory authority.
Sources: NSA's Bulk Collection Of Americans' Phone Data Is Illegal, Appeals Court Rules (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2015/05/07/404898259/federal-court-bulk-collection-of-phone-metadata-is-illegal> ; Report on the Telephone Records Program Conducted under Section 215 (Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board) <https://documents.pclob.gov/prod/Documents/OversightReport/ec542143-1079-424a-84b3-acc354698560/215-Report_on_the_Telephone_Records_Program.pdf>

Description: GM recalled millions of vehicles over a defective ignition switch linked to at least 124 deaths; engineers knew of the switch defect before production, and the company delayed disclosure and recall after recognizing its airbag-safety implications.
Structural_Note: A known defect linked to deaths went undisclosed for years before recall.
Sources: U.S. Attorney Announces Criminal Charges Against General Motors and Deferred Prosecution Agreement (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://justice.gov/opa/pr/us-attorney-southern-district-new-york-announces-criminal-charges-against-general-motors-and> ; GM Ignition Switch Deaths Total 124 As Fund Nears Completion (Associated Press, via CBS News Detroit) <https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/gm-ignition-switch-deaths-total-124-as-fund-nears-completion/>

Authority: State of Michigan (emergency managers) / MDEQ / EPA
Description: A state-directed switch in water source, without corrosion control, exposed Flint residents to lead and bacteria; officials downplayed the danger.
Structural_Note: A state-directed water-source change exposed residents to lead; official responses to early warnings were delayed.
Sources: Flint Water Advisory Task Force Final Report, March 2016 (State of Michigan) <https://www.michigan.gov/-/media/Project/Websites/formergovernors/Folder6/FWATF_FINAL_REPORT_21March2016.pdf?rev=284b9e42c7c840019109eb73aaeedb68> ; Flint water crisis (Encyclopaedia Britannica) <https://www.britannica.com/event/Flint-water-crisis>

Description: VW installed software that detected emissions tests and reduced emissions controls in normal driving on about 590,000 U.S. diesel cars, so they emitted far more pollution than reported; the company later pleaded guilty in US federal court.
Structural_Note: Software designed to defeat emissions tests increased pollution beyond reported levels; later adjudicated.
Sources: Volkswagen AG Agrees to Plead Guilty and Pay $4.3 Billion in Criminal and Civil Penalties (U.S. Department of Justice) <https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/volkswagen-ag-agrees-plead-guilty-and-pay-43-billion-criminal-and-civil-penalties-six> ; Learn About Volkswagen Violations (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, archived) <https://19january2017snapshot.epa.gov/vw/learn-about-volkswagen-violations_.html>

Description: Employees opened millions of accounts without customers' authorization to meet sales quotas, and some customers were charged fees as a result; the company later paid settlements to federal regulators.
Structural_Note: Sales-quota pressure resulted in millions of unauthorized customer accounts.
Sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Fines Wells Fargo $100 Million for Widespread Illegal Practice of Secretly Opening Unauthorized Accounts (CFPB) <https://www.consumerfinance.gov/archive/newsroom/consumer-financial-protection-bureau-fines-wells-fargo-100-million-widespread-illegal-practice-secretly-opening-unauthorized-accounts/> ; Enforcement action: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. (2016) (CFPB) <https://www.consumerfinance.gov/enforcement/actions/wells-fargo-bank-2016/>

Description: A breach exposed sensitive personal data of about 147 million people; the company had failed to patch a known vulnerability.
Structural_Note: A custodian of consumers' sensitive data left a known vulnerability unpatched; ~147M people were exposed.
Sources: Equifax to Pay $575 Million as Part of Settlement with FTC, CFPB, and States Related to 2017 Data Breach (Federal Trade Commission) <https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2019/07/equifax-pay-575-million-part-settlement-ftc-cfpb-states-related-2017-data-breach> ; Data Protection: Actions Taken by Equifax and Federal Agencies in Response to the 2017 Breach, GAO-18-559 (U.S. Government Accountability Office) <https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-18-559>

Authority: Department of Homeland Security / Department of Justice
Description: A policy of prosecuting border crossers led to thousands of children being separated from parents, many without adequate tracking to reunite them.
Structural_Note: Families were separated without reliable tracking or reunification procedures; some children had not been confirmed reunited with their families, and the harms of separation could persist even where reunification occurred.
Sources: DHS Lacked Technology Needed to Successfully Account for Separated Migrant Families, OIG-20-06 (DHS Office of Inspector General) <https://www.oig.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/assets/2019-11/OIG-20-06-Nov19.pdf> ; Separated Children Placed in Office of Refugee Resettlement Care (HHS Office of Inspector General) <https://www.oig.hhs.gov/reports/all/2019/separated-children-placed-in-office-of-refugee-resettlement-care/>

Description: A wildfire ignited by worn utility transmission equipment destroyed the town of Paradise, California and killed 84 people, according to prosecutors; the utility later pleaded guilty.
Structural_Note: Worn utility equipment ignited a fatal wildfire; the utility later pleaded guilty.
Sources: Camp Fire (Butte County District Attorney, Butte County, CA) <https://www.buttecounty.net/342/Camp-Fire> ; PG&E Pleads Guilty On 2018 California Camp Fire: 'Our Equipment Started That Fire' (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/2020/06/16/879008760/pg-e-pleads-guilty-on-2018-california-camp-fire-our-equipment-started-that-fire>

Description: Two crashes tied to flawed flight-control software killed 346 people; reviews found Boeing concealed information and the FAA delegated too much oversight to Boeing.
Structural_Note: Reviews found the safety regulator had delegated oversight to the firm it was meant to check.
Sources: After 18-Month Investigation, Chairs Release Final Committee Report on Boeing 737 MAX (U.S. House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure) <https://democrats-transportation.house.gov/news/press-releases/after-18-month-investigation-chairs-defazio-and-larsen-release-final-committee-report-on-boeing-737-max> ; Congressional Inquiry Faults Boeing And FAA Failures For Deadly 737 Max Plane Crashes (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/2020/09/16/913426448/congressional-inquiry-faults-boeing-and-faa-failures-for-deadly-737-max-plane-cr>

Description: A train carrying hazardous chemicals derailed in East Palestine, Ohio; chemicals were released and burned, including in a vent and burn of vinyl chloride the NTSB later found unnecessary, and residents were evacuated.
Structural_Note: Inadequate hazard detection preceded the derailment; incomplete and misleading information to emergency decision-makers contributed to an unnecessary chemical release and burn.
Sources: Failed Wheel Bearing Caused Norfolk Southern Train Derailment in East Palestine, Ohio (National Transportation Safety Board) <https://www.ntsb.gov/news/press-releases/Pages/NR20240625.aspx> ; Norfolk Southern Railway Derailment and Hazardous Materials Release, RIR-24-05 (National Transportation Safety Board) <https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/RIR2405%20CORRECTED.pdf>

Description: Poor interest-rate risk management triggered what was then the second-largest U.S. bank failure (third-largest after May 2023); supervisors had flagged but not resolved the weaknesses.
Structural_Note: Interest-rate risk and supervisory gaps preceded the failure, affecting depositors and the wider system.
Sources: Review of the Federal Reserve's Supervision and Regulation of Silicon Valley Bank, April 2023: Key Takeaways (Federal Reserve Board) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2023-April-SVB-Key-Takeaways.htm> ; FDIC: Historical Timeline (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation) <https://www.fdic.gov/90years>

Description: A door plug blew out mid-flight after four securing bolts were left missing during manufacturing; the NTSB found failures in Boeing's training, documentation, and quality oversight, with ineffective FAA oversight contributing to the accident.
Structural_Note: Recurring production-quality failures, after earlier crashes, again exposed the flying public to risk.
Sources: In-flight structural failure, Alaska Airlines Flight 1282, investigation DCA24MA063 (National Transportation Safety Board) <https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/Pages/DCA24MA063.aspx> ; NTSB blames Boeing in 737 Max door plug blowout (NPR) <https://www.npr.org/2025/06/24/nx-s1-5442564/ntsb-boeing-737-max-door-plug-alaska-airlines>
